FAKTORY RISKA SOSUDISTOI KAL'TSIFIKATSII
Povyshennyi uroven' glikemii

Dostatochnoe kolichestvo issledovanii posviashcheno mekhanizmam patogeneza KS vsledstvie khronicheskoi giperglikemii. Ustanovleno, chto in vitro GMKS, kul'tiviruemye v usloviiakh povyshennogo urovnia gliukozy, ekspressiruiut RANX2, BMP-2 i osteokal'tsin. V rabote, provedennoi na myshinykh GMK, vysokii uroven' gliukozy sposobstvoval ikh prevrashcheniiu v osteoblasty s vysokoi ekspressiei dekorina.

Osnovnaia funktsiia dekorina vkliuchaet reguliatsiiu vo vremia kletochnogo tsikla. Ekzogennyi dekorin ingibiruet aktivnost' fermentov, razrushaiushchikh vnekletochnyi matriks i degradatsiiu kollagena, odnovremenno aktiviruia otlozhenie matriksa i usilivaia kal'tsifikatsiiu. Analogichno v issledovaniiakh in vitro bylo pokazano, chto vysokii uroven' gliukozy vyzyvaet kal'tsifikatsiiu GMKS.

Pri vozdeistvii okislitel'nogo stressa na GMKS v usloviiakh povyshennogo urovnia gliukozy i drugikh stimuliruiushchikh faktorov oni differentsiruiutsia v osteoblastopodobnye kletki i sekretiruiut bol'shoe kolichestvo belkov kostnoi tkani. R. Kawakami i soavt. obnaruzhili, chto semeistvo belkov S100 u bol'nykh SD tesno sviazano s KS.

Giperglikemiia sposobstvuet uvelicheniiu sekretsii S100A9 i povysheniiu ekspressii belkovykh retseptorov RAGE. V srede s vysokim soderzhaniem gliukozy provospalitel'nye makrofagi vysvobozhdaiut kal'tsinirovannye vnekletochnye vezikuly, kotorye formiruiut ateroskleroticheskie mikrokal'tsifikaty cherez os' S100A9-RAGE.

Gliukozozavisimaia produktsiia mitokhondrial'nogo superoksida stanovitsia chrezmernoi, chto privodit k aktivatsii NF-kappaB. IAdernyi faktor NF-kappaB predstavliaet znachimyi transkriptsionnyi faktor, aktiviruiushchii mnogie provospalitel'nye mekhanizmy v razvitii ateroskleroza i mediakal'tsinoza. RAGE, retseptor k konechnym produktam glikirovaniia, pri vzaimodeistvii s belkami gruppy S100A zapuskaet kaskad reaktsii, kotoryi sposobstvuet uvelicheniiu transkriptsii iadernogo faktora NF-kappaB i povysheniiu urovnia aktivnykh form kisloroda, chto vedet k razvitiiu lokal'nogo oksidativnogo stressa. Sviazyvanie RAGE s ligandom stimuliruet produktsiiu osnovnykh provospalitel'nykh tsitokinov : IL-6, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha. Eti markery takzhe stimuliruiut lokal'noe vospalenie v neskol'kikh tipakh kletok: endotelial'nykh, gladkomyshechnykh kletkakh sosudistoi stenki, leikotsitakh. S100A9 povyshaet sekretsiiu provospalitel'nykh tsitokinov s pomoshch'iu takikh mekhanizmov, kak obrazovanie aktivnykh form kisloroda i aktivatsiia chuvstvitel'nykh k nim transkriptsionnykh faktorov (NF-kappaB). Giperglikemiia sposobstvuet takzhe povyshennoi ekspressii belkov BMP -2/4. U bol'nykh SD povyshena ekspressiia BMP -2/4 v aorte. Etot belok sposobstvuet osteogennoi differentsirovke GMKS, chto privodit k ikh kal'tsifikatsii.
Narushenie obmena lipidov

Pitanie s povyshennym soderzhaniem zhirov, osobenno zhivotnogo proiskhozhdeniia, sposobstvuet razvitiiu ozhireniia, arterial'noi gipertenzii i SD. U patsientov s SD okislennye lipoproteiny nizkoi plotnosti (LPNP) vnosiat vklad v progressirovanie ateroskleroza i kal'tsifikatsiiu srednei obolochki arterii (medii). Krupnoe observatsionnoe issledovanie patsientov s SD1 v shvedskoi klinicheskoi praktike pokazalo, chto kazhdoe povyshenie urovnia kholesterina LPNP na 1 mmol'/l privodit k povysheniiu riska serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii (SSZ) na 9% u lits, ne poluchavshikh terapiiu statinami. V issledovanii byl sdelan vyvod o tom, chto kholesterin LPNP, po-vidimomu, ne iavliaetsia dostatochno tochnym markerom serdechno-sosudistogo riska pri pervichnoi profilaktike u patsientov s SD1 . Evropeiskoe issledovanie oslozhnenii insulinozavisimogo SD (EURODIAB IDDM Complications Study) takzhe pokazalo, chto kholesterin LPNP ne iavliaetsia prediktorom serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii. Tem ne menee standarty meditsinskoi pomoshchi Amerikanskoi assotsiatsii diabeta (ADA : American Diabetes Association) predpolagaiut, chto uroven' kholesterina LPNP sostavliaet 2,6 mmol'/l i bolee iavliaetsia markerom povyshennogo serdechno-sosudistogo riska. Issledovaniia in vitro pokazali, chto lipoproteiny vysokoi plotnosti (LPVP) ne podvergaiutsia okisleniiu i okazyvaiut protektivnoe deistvie na arterial'nuiu stenku blagodaria ingibiruiushchemu deistviiu na KS. Giperglikemiia, po-vidimomu, okazyvaet bolee sushchestvennoe vliianie na serdechno-sosudistye riski pri SD1, chem pri SD2. V modeliakh prognozirovaniia riskov dlia patsientov s SD1 obshchii kholesterin i kholesterin LPVP bolee vazhny, chem kholesterin LPNP v otsenke prognoza neblagopriiatnykh serdechno-sosudistykh iskhodov. Vazhno otmetit', chto kazhushchiesia normal'nymi kontsentratsii kholesterina v syvorotke krovi, chasto nabliudaemye pri SD1, skryvaiut aterogennyi lipidnyi profil' s povyshennym soderzhaniem lipoproteinov promezhutochnoi (srednei) plotnosti LPPP i LPNP, a takzhe disfunktsional'nykh LPVP. Povyshennyi uroven' apolipoproteina A-1 (apo A1), soderzhashchegosia v LPVP, iavliaetsia nezavisimym geneticheski determinirovannym prichinnym faktorom riska razvitiia serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii. Vliianie SD1 na uroven' apo A1 neiasno, no prospektivnoe observatsionnoe issledovanie pokazalo, chto ego uroven', prevyshaiushchii 30 mg/dl, mozhet imet' znachenie dlia prognozirovaniia serdechno-sosudistykh sobytii u patsientov s SD1 . Interesno, chto intensivnoe lechenie v issledovanii DCCT (Diabetes Control and Complications Trial) bylo sviazano so snizheniem apo A1, a takzhe apo V . Snizhenie urovnia LPVP chasto soprovozhdaetsia povysheniem urovnia leptina v krovoobrashchenii. Vysokii uroven' leptina, v svoiu ochered', aktiviruet osteogennyi signal'nyi put' BMP, stimuliruia differentsirovku GMKS v osteoblasty i oposreduet KS. Razmer chastits LPNP, ikh glikirovanie i okislenie sviazany s vysokim riskom SSZ. Lipoproteiny ochen' nizkoi plotnosti (LPONP) legche pronikaiut v stenku arterii, chem LPNP, bolee vospriimchivy k okislitel'nomu stressu, imeiut dlitel'nyi period poluvyvedeniia iz plazmy i obladaiut snizhennym srodstvom k sviazyvaniiu s retseptorami LPNP. Proudfood D. i soavt. otmetili, chto pri razvitii dislipidemii atsetilirovannye LPNP uvelichivaiut osteogennyi fenotip GMKS v 3 raza. Takim obrazom, LPNP indutsiruiut ikh differentsirovku i povyshaiut aktivnost' shchelochnoi fosfatazy. Naprotiv, LPVP ingibiruiut put' osteogennoi differentsirovki GMKS. Krome togo, giperkholesterinemiia usilivaet okislitel'nyi stress i uskoriaet KS, indutsirovannuiu vitaminom D. Bjornstad R. i soavt. ustanovili, chto gipertriglitseridemiia predstavliaet nezavisimyi prognosticheskii faktor progressirovaniia kal'tsifikatsii koronarnykh arterii u patsientov s SD. Nekotorye issledovaniia pokazali, chto giperlipidemiia sviazana s narusheniem provedeniia signalov na odnom iz ego etapov po puti Wnt/beta-katenin, kotoryi igraet vazhnuiu rol' v KS.
Izmenenie urovnia insulina

V fiziologicheskikh usloviiakh insulin okazyvaet angioprotektivnoe deistvie pri razvitii kal'tsinoza. Mnogochislennye issledovaniia pokazali, chto oksid azota (NO) ingibiruet aktivatsiiu trombotsitov i ogranichivaet migratsiiu i proliferatsiiu GMKS. Insulin stimuliruet endotelii sosudov k vysvobozhdeniiu NO, kotoryi vposledstvii okisliaet lipoproteiny, tem samym snizhaia skorost' kal'tsifikatsii intimy i prepiatstvuia osteogennoi differentsirovke GMKS.

Povyshennaia sekretsiia insulina assotsiirovana s insulinorezistentnost'iu (IR). Insulinorezistentnost', po-vidimomu, predskazyvaet stepen' razvitiia KS i mozhet byt' sviazana s bolee vysokim riskom serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii, osobenno u patsientov s SD. V sluchae insulinorezistentnosti v pechen' postupaet bol'shoe kolichestvo svobodnykh zhirnykh kislot. Pri etom organizm kompensiruet eto sostoianie izbytochnym pogloshcheniem triglitseridov pechen'iu, a takzhe obrazovaniem i sekretsiei LPONP, chto soprovozhdaetsia povysheniem riska KS. Kak pokazano v issledovanii T. Iguchi i soavt., patsienty s bolee vysokim urovnem IR sklonny k massivnym fibroznym ateroskleroticheskim nasloeniiam v sosudakh tonkoi kishki. IR sposobstvuet razvitiiu ateroskleroza, indutsiruia vospalitel'nuiu aktivnost' krovenosnykh sosudov i immunnykh kletok. Kak bylo pokazano Queralt Martin-Saladich i soavt., chem vyshe indeks IR, tem vyshe kal'tsifikatsiia koronarnykh arterii. V drugom issledovanii, provedennom s uchastiem 1632 patsientov bez SD, bylo pokazano, chto IR sviazana tol'ko s kal'tsinozom koronarnykh arterii, no ne aorty.

Kletki Kupfera iavliaiutsia rezidentnymi makrofagami pecheni i igraiut vazhnuiu rol' v podderzhanii funktsii pecheni. V sluchae giperinsulinemii klirens kletok Kupfera v pecheni umen'shaetsia. Eto izmenenie privodit k snizheniiu klirensa lipopolisakharidov, absorbiruiushchikhsia iz ZHKT, i sootvetstvuiushchemu uvelicheniiu tsirkuliruiushchikh urovnei lipopolisakharidov i insulina. Krome togo, v issledovanii na krysakh ingibirovanie kletok Kupfera vyzyvalo povyshenie urovnia gliukozy v organizme i stimulirovalo chrezmernuiu sekretsiiu insulina, privodia k IR. Stefan N. i soavt. vyiavili, chto plazmennyi globulin A ingibiruet peredachu signala insulina i indutsiruet IR, chto privodit k aterosklerozu.
Ozhirenie

Ozhirenie iavliaetsia nezavisimym faktorom riska razvitiia serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii. Naibolee chasto izbytochnyi ves vstrechaetsia sredi patsientov s SD2, v to vremia kak rasprostranennost' ozhireniia u patsientov s SD1 ne vyshe, chem u naseleniia v tselom. U patsientov s SD1 ozhirenie assotsiirovano s nalichiem i progressirovaniem kal'tsinoza koronarnykh arterii, mezhdu tem sviaz' mezhdu ozhireniem i SD2 v nastoiashchee vremia ne do kontsa izuchena. V Britanskom issledovanii bylo pokazano, chto u patsientov s SD2 smertnost' ot vsekh prichin byla vyshe u patsientov s indeksom massy tela (IMT) 35-54 kg/m2 i 20-24 kg/m2. V nedavnem otechestvennom issledovanii byla prodemonstrirovana vysokaia rasprostranennost' ishemicheskoi bolezni serdtsa u patsientov s vistseral'nym ozhireniem i kal'tsifikatsiei koronarnykh arterii. Vmeste s etim, po dannym riada issledovanii, vyiavlena vzaimosviaz' mezhdu ob''emom epikardial'noi zhirovoi tkani, iavliaiushcheisia gormonal'no-aktivnym obrazovaniem i kal'tsinozom koronarnykh arterii. Vzaimodeistvie mezhdu epikardial'noi zhirovoi tkan'iu i koronarnymi arteriiami proiskhodit cherez parakrinnuiu aktivnost', vkliuchaiushchuiu markery vospaleniia, kotorye mogut oposredovat' i indutsirovat' kal'tsifikatsiiu. V issledovanii, v kotorom priniali uchastie 1414 afroamerikantsev, kal'tsinoz koronarnykh arterii i kal'tsinoz abdominal'noi aorty byli assotsiirovany s epikardial'nym zhirom.
Arterial'naia gipertenziia

Renin-angiotenzin-al'dosteronovaia sistema (RAAS) iavliaetsia osnovnym patogeneticheskim faktorom, sposobstvuiushchim apoptozu, rostu i differentsirovke GMKS, chto pozvoliaet predpolozhit' vozmozhnoe uchastie etoi sistemy v KS. Angiotenzin II sposobstvuet differentsirovke GMKS v osteoblasty putem aktivatsii RANKL. Analogichnym putem povyshenie aktivnosti al'dosterona soprovozhdaetsia povysheniem arterial'nogo davleniia i progressirovaniem serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii. Pri povyshenii urovnia al'dosterona v krovi aktiviruiutsia faktory vospaleniia i proliferatsii, negativno vliiaia na sostoianie arterii.

Issledovaniia takzhe pokazali, chto promotornaia posledovatel'nost' gena pit-1, kotoryi iavliaetsia gipofizarno-spetsificheskim faktorom transkriptsii, mozhet soderzhat' elementy raspoznavaniia mikroRNK na svoikh tselevykh messendzhernykh RNK. MikroRNK, kotorye predstavliaiut soboi ochen' korotkie nekodiruiushchie RNK, igraiut vazhnuiu rol' v reguliatsii ekspressii genov i progressirovanii zabolevaniia. V dannom sluchae rech' idet o vliianii povyshennogo urovnia al'dosterona na osteoinduktsiiu cherez pit-1. Pit-1 reguliruet pogloshchenie fosfata i neobkhodim dlia fenotipicheskoi transformatsii i kal'tsifikatsii GMKS. X. Li i soavt. ustanovili, chto podavlenie pit-1 malykh interferiruiushchikh RNK snizhalo urovni matrichnoi RNK Cbfa1 (semeistvo transkriptsionnykh faktorov, izvestnykh takzhe pod nazvaniiami Runx2 ili Osf-2, osteoblast specific transcription factor 2, osteoblast-spetsificheskii faktor transkriptsii 2) i SHCHF i ingibirovalo kal'tsifikatsiiu sosudov.

Takim obrazom, disreguliatsiia RAAS tesno sviazana s KS. Eto delaet RAAS privlekatel'noi terapevticheskoi mishen'iu dlia razrabotki effektivnykh metodov farmakoterapii mediakal'tsinoza pri serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevaniiakh.
Zabolevaniia pochek

Epidemiologicheskie issledovaniia pokazali, chto u patsientov s SD veroiatnost' razvitiia KHBP primerno v dva raza vyshe, chem u liudei bez narusheniia uglevodnogo obmena. Issledovanie M. Wang i soavt. patsientov s terminal'noi stadiei KHPN, poluchaiushchikh terapiiu programmnym gemodializom, pokazalo, chto rasprostranennost' KS u nikh sostavila 77,4%. CHastota kal'tsinoza koronarnykh arterii u nedializnykh patsientov s SD2 s porazheniem pochek byla vyshe, chem u patsientov s SD2 bez povrezhdeniia pochek (95 i 59%), a mediana otsenki koronarnogo kal'tsiia byla znachitel'no vyshe. Po mere progressirovaniia KHPN vozrastaet veroiatnost' narusheniia metabolizma kal'tsiia i fosfora, predstavliaia dopolnitel'nyi risk kal'tsinoza. Vneskeletnaia kal'tsifikatsiia chasto vstrechaetsia u patsientov s KHBP; ee rasprostranennost' uvelichivaetsia po mere narastaniia KHPN i uvelicheniia prodolzhitel'nosti dializa.

Kliuchevuiu rol' v razvitii KS igraet provospalitel'noe okruzhenie v sistemnom krovoobrashchenii, kharakterizuiushcheesia nepreryvnym povysheniem soderzhaniia vospalitel'nykh belkov i tsitokinov, chasto vstrechaiushcheesia u patsientov s khronicheskim zabolevaniem pochek. Nebol'shoe uvelichenie etikh pokazatelei polozhitel'no korreliruet s aktivatorami kal'tsifikatsii.
Protsess stareniia

Soglasno dannym literatury, starenie sposobstvuet KS putem aktivatsii riada protsessov: osteogennoi transformatsii gladkomyshechnykh kletok, vysvobozhdeniiu vezikul endotelial'nymi kletkami, remodelirovaniiu vnekletochnogo matriksa, disbalansu metabolizma fosfora, povrezhdeniiu DNK, vospalitel'noi reaktsii i snizheniiu ekspressii antivozrastnykh faktorov.

V to zhe vremia u pozhilykh liudei usilivaetsia sochetannoe vozdeistvie na arterial'nuiu stenku drugikh negativnykh faktorov. Tak, naprimer, kolichestvo KPG, soderzhashchikhsia v tkaniakh u patsientov s SD2, po mere stareniia bol'she, chem u patsientov bez SD. Pri giperglikemii signaly AGE/RAGE peredaiutsia cherez PKC (proteinkinaza S, PKC : protein kinase C), p38 MAPK (mitogen-aktiviruemye proteinkinazy, p38 : mitogen-activated protein kinases), TGF-beta (transformiruiushchii faktor rosta beta, TGFbeta1 : transforming growth factor beta1) i vnutrikletochnyi signal'nyi put' NF-kappaB (iadernyi faktor kappa v, NF-kappaB : nuclear factor kappaB), a takzhe drugie signal'nye puti, kotorye uvelichivaiut kolichestvo belkov kostnogo matriksa.

Bolee togo, bylo pokazano, chto peredacha signalov AGE/RAGE uvelichivaet okislitel'nyi stress i sposobstvuet KS, oposredovannoi SD, putem aktivatsii Nox-1 (NADPH-oksidaza (NOX)) i snizheniia ekspressii gena SOD-1 .
GISTOPATOLOGIIA MEDIAKAL'TSINOZA

Mediakal'tsinoz rasprostraniaetsia preimushchestvenno na arterii myshechnogo tipa, k kotorym otnosiatsia sosudy srednego i melkogo kalibrov. V stenkakh etikh arterii imeetsia otnositel'no bol'shoe kolichestvo GMK. Ranniaia stadiia obyzvestvleniia srednei obolochki arterii kharakterizuetsia poiavleniem kristallov fosfata kal'tsiia v promezhutochnom veshchestve okolo elasticheskikh volokon. Na pozdnikh stadiiakh razvitiia mediakal'tsinoza nabliudaetsia formirovanie massivnykh progressiruiushchikh ochagov otlozheniia solei kal'tsiia v srednei obolochke vdol' elasticheskikh volokon, chto soprovozhdaetsia fragmentatsiei vnutrennei elasticheskoi membrany.

Issledovaniia poslednikh let ukazyvaiut na sochetannye patologicheskie izmeneniia intimy i medii u patsientov s diabeticheskoi makroangiopatiei s preimushchestvennym porazheniem srednei obolochki arterii. Otsenka obraztsov gistologicheskikh srezov materialov amputirovannykh konechnostei u bol'nykh s diabeticheskoi nefropatiei pokazala, chto neateromatoznoe intimal'noe utolshchenie stenok arterii (otsutstvie lipidov i makrofagov) samo po sebe mozhet privesti k znachitel'nomu stenozu, a inogda : k okkliuzii ili trombozu.

V drugom issledovanii gistologicheskii analiz operatsionnogo materiala konechnostei u patsientov s SD2 (80%), terminal'noi stadiei KHBP (48,3%) i ZANK vyiavil priznaki vyrazhennogo (bolee 50%) tsirkuliarnogo i polisegmentarnogo kal'tsinoza srednei obolochki arterii, a takzhe ateroskleroticheskoe porazhenie s formirovaniem znachimykh stenozov.

Rezul'taty patomorfologicheskikh issledovanii operatsionnogo materiala konechnostei bol'nykh SD i ZANK ustanovili tesnuiu sviaz' mezhdu vyrazhennoi giperplaziei intimy, progressiruiushchim mediakal'tsinozom, rasprostraniaiushchimsia na arterii goleni i stopy, i razvitiem tromboticheskikh okkliuzii.

Takim obrazom, osnovnym elementom diabeticheskoi makroangiopatii iavliaetsia porazhenie srednei obolochki arterii : medii myshechnykh arterii, kotoroe mozhet soprovozhdat'sia takzhe patologiei intimy.
V tselom, poluchennye na segodniashnii den' dannye o gistopatologii mediakal'tsinoza svidetel'stvuiut o ego znachitel'nom vklade v razvitie i progressirovanie ZANK u patsientov s SD.
ZAKLIUCHENIE

Mediakal'tsinoz arterii iavliaetsia rasprostranennym oslozhneniem u patsientov s SD i odnoi iz vazhneishikh prichin serdechno-sosudistykh zabolevanii i smerti. Protsessy i mekhanizmy KS iavliaiutsia slozhno reguliruemym patofiziologicheskim fenomenom, oposredovannym razlichnymi kletkami, kotoryi kharakterizuetsia transformatsiei GMKS iz ikh pervonachal'nogo sokratitel'nogo fenotipa v osteoblastopodobnyi fenotip posle stimuliatsii razlichnymi pro- i antikal'tsifitsiruiushchimi faktorami. Vazhneishuiu rol' sredi faktorov riska pri SD igraiut khronicheskaia giperglikemiia i oksidativnyi stress, a v sluchae soputstvuiushchei KHPN, osobenno u patsientov, nakhodiashchikhsia na dialize, puskovym mekhanizmom iavliaetsia narushenie fosforno-kal'tsievogo obmena. Dopolnitel'nymi faktorami riska razvitiia mediakal'tsinoza iavliaiutsia takie patologicheskie sostoianiia, kak giperinsulinemiia i insulinorezistentnost', narushenie obmena lipidov, ozhirenie, disreguliatsiia RAAS pri arterial'noi gipertenzii i starenie. V nastoiashchee vremia formiruetsia ponimanie mnogogrannosti vzaimodeistviia etikh patologicheskikh protsessov, a takzhe ikh kliniko-prognosticheskoi roli. Glubokoe znanie aspektov patogeneza mediakal'tsinoza mozhet lech' v osnovu razrabotki meropriiatii po ego profilaktike u patsientov s SD i nametit' tseli farmakologicheskoi terapii u bol'nykh s uzhe razvivshimsia zabolevaniem.
DOPOLNITEL'NAIA INFORMATSIIA
Istochniki finansirovaniia. Rabota vypolnena po initsiative avtorov bez privlecheniia finansirovaniia.
Konflikt interesov. Avtory deklariruiut otsutstvie iavnykh i potentsial'nykh konfliktov interesov, sviazannykh s soderzhaniem nastoiashchei stat'i.

Uchastie avtorov. Vse avtory odobrili final'nuiu versiiu stat'i pered publikatsiei, vyrazili soglasie nesti otvetstvennost' za vse aspekty raboty, podrazumevaiushchuiu nadlezhashchee izuchenie i reshenie voprosov, sviazannykh s tochnost'iu ili dobrosovestnost'iu liuboi chasti raboty.

passages.text: Biosimilar insulins: Narrative review of the regulatory framework and registration studies
Abstract

Biosimilar insulins have been commercially available in the EU since 2014. Currently, six biosimilar insulins are approved in the EU and four in the US. However, commercial success has been limited, which may be in part due to concerns among physicians and people with diabetes that biosimilar insulins are substandard in efficacy, safety, and quality compared to reference products. Indeed, unlike generic drugs, which are identical chemical copies of their reference counterparts, in a biological manufacturing process, subtle differences can arise between products, even if the tertiary molecular structures are the same. Therefore, there is a clear regulatory pathway for the approval of biosimilars. For biosimilar insulins, preclinical (hormone receptor and cell) studies are needed to investigate potential differences in the response to biosimilar insulins and their reference medicinal products. In addition, there is a requirement for pivotal clinical pharmacology studies involving the euglycaemic glucose clamp technique to investigate comparative time-action profiles, whereas later-phase clinical safety, efficacy, and immunogenicity studies usually are no longer needed for the approval of biosimilar insulins. This narrative review provides an overview of pivotal phase 1 clamp and supportive larger phase 3 studies that supported the registration of biosimilar insulins in the EU and US, and discusses the need for interchangeability and immunogenicity studies. Overall, the current regulatory approach in the EU and in the USA ensures that there are no relevant differences between biosimilar insulins and their reference products. Therefore, people with diabetes and prescribers can use EU or US approved biosimilars without any concerns.
Plain Language Summary

Six biosimilar insulins are approved by the EU regulator, the European Medicines Agency, and are currently available on the EU market. Three biosimilar insulins are approved by the US regulator, the Food and Drugs Agency, and are currently available on the US market. However, commercial success has been limited, which may be in part due to concerns among physicians and people with diabetes that biosimilar insulins are perhaps not quite the same as the original products with respect to efficacy, safety, and quality.

Such concerns could be valid, because unlike generic drugs, which are identical chemical copies of their reference counterparts, biosimilar protein biosimilar and originator drugs cannot be chemically identical. In a biological manufacturing process, subtle difference can and will arise between products, even if the tertiary molecular structures, that is the amino acid sequence, the interactions between different parts of the protein and the three-dimensional folding, are the same. To assure that these unavoidable subtle differences do not result in differences in efficacy, safety and quality, there is a clear regulatory pathway for the approval of biosimilars. In addition to chemical studies, preclinical studies are needed to investigate potential differences in the response to biosimilar insulins and their reference medicinal products. These include e.g. studies investigating affinity to the insulin receptor, and how the insulins induce their effect in cell models. Next, pivotal clinical pharmacology studies involving the euglycaemic glucose clamp technique to investigate comparative time action profiles are required. Later phase clinical safety, efficacy and immunogenicity studies usually are no longer needed for the approval of biosimilar insulins.

This narrative review provides an overview of pivotal phase 1 clamp and supportive larger phase 3 studies which supported registration of biosimilar insulins in the EU and US, and discusses the need for interchangeability and immunogenicity studies. Overall, the current regulatory approach in the EU and in the USA ensures that there are no relevant differences between biosimilar insulins and their reference products. Therefore, people with diabetes and prescribers can use EU or US approved biosimilars without any concerns.
INTRODUCTION

The first approved biosimilar product, a growth hormone, received a positive opinion by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in 2006. This was based on a legal framework introduced in 2004. To date, more than 100 biosimilars have been approved in the EU. These are mainly low-molecular weight heparins, growth factors, hormones, and monoclonal antibodies. Among the hormones are eight insulins, the first being approved in the EU in 2014.

Although offered at lower costs than reference products, the commercial success of biosimilar insulins has been limited. In 2021, the total market share of biosimilar insulins was only 8% in the EU and about 10% in the USA. The relatively slow uptake of biosimilar insulin might be, at least in part, due to concerns among patients and health care providers 'that biosimilars are substandard in efficacy, safety, and quality to the reference product, similar to how some patients perceive generics as inferior to the branded counterpart'.

Indeed, as outlined below, there are subtle differences between biosimilars and their reference products which, at least theoretically, could lead to differences in safety, efficacy, and the immunogenic (i.e., antibody) response. On the other hand, insulin is a relatively simple biologic compared to, for example, growth hormone and monoclonal antibodies, and slight differences to the reference product might not be of clinical relevance. It is therefore important to understand how the legal approval frameworks, for example, in the EU and the USA, ensure the safety and efficacy of biosimilar insulins. Can clinicians and people with diabetes place their full trust in biosimilar insulins?
Biosimilars are not bioidentical

The EMA defines a biosimilar as follows: 'A biosimilar is a biological medicine highly similar to another already approved biological medicine (the "reference medicine")'. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) uses a very akin definition, and adds that there should be 'no clinically meaningful differences from an existing FDA-approved reference product'. In contrast to generics, biosimilars are expected to be similar rather than identical, because some variability is inherent in the manufacture of biological medicines. While the primary, secondary and tertiary structures of biosimilar insulins are usually identical to those of reference insulins, differences in critical quality attributes might be introduced by different manufacturing processes. The typical insulin-manufacturing process is done by isolation of genes that are inserted into a host cell (usually bacteria such as Escherichia coli or (nowadays much more common) yeast), establishment and expansion of cell lines to produce the insulin, isolation, purification, formulation, packaging and distribution through a cold-chain distribution channel. Manufacturing processes are proprietary, so insulin preparations will always differ with regard to cell lines, isolation and purification processes, etc. These differences in the manufacturing process will result in differences with regard to, for example, oxidation, impurities, and glycosylation. One example for slight differences in glycosylation is shown in Figure 1.

Reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography of Basalog (blue line) and originator Lantus indicating slight different glycosylation patterns for the two insulins. AU, arbitrary units. Reproduced from Reference.

As there will always be differences between biosimilar and reference insulins as well as even between batches of the same insulin, regulations have to be in place to ensure that these variations do not affect the insulin's biological activity or immunogenicity.
Regulatory framework

Biosimilars are approved according to the same standards of pharmaceutical quality, safety, and efficacy that apply to all biological medicines. In particular, the highest manufacturing standards, as demanded by good manufacturing practice (GMP) guidelines, have to be implemented, similar to the demands for all other pharmaceuticals. Adherence to these standards is ensured not only by a thorough review of the documentation on the manufacturing process and entire pharmaceutical development but also by inspections of the manufacturing site by regulatory agencies. Thus, manufacturing standards are the same for biosimilar and reference insulins.
comparative analytical and functional studies
comparative pre-clinical studies
comparative clinical studies

To investigate the degree of similarity between a biosimilar and a reference product, regulatory agencies look at the totality of evidence for comparative function, purity, potency, and safety. In order to show similarity, three types of studies have to be submitted to the regulatory agency:

Comparative means that the biosimilar product is directly compared to the reference. The analytical and functional studies should confirm the primary structure (amino acid sequence) of the biosimilar, but also its secondary and higher-order structures, as well as post-translational modifications. Comparative pre-clinical studies look at receptor binding and activation in cells. For insulin, this includes binding studies to the insulin A and B receptors, also investigating on-off kinetics. Assessment of insulin's metabolic activity needs to include glycogen formation, lipogenesis, and inhibition of stimulated lipolysis, as well as glucose transport in cell studies. Pharmacodynamic studies in animal models are not expected to be sensitive enough to detect differences not identified by in vitro assays and are therefore not required for insulins. In vivo toxicological studies are only required in certain cases, for example, when the biosimilar is produced in a new type of cell or organism, or when the formulation includes novel excipients not used previously.
Comparative clinical studies

As mentioned above, so far eight biosimilar insulins have been approved in the EU: three insulin glargine products; two insulin aspart products; one insulin lispro product; one human insulin product, and one pre-mixed insulin. In addition, two were withdrawn after approval: a human insulin product and a glargine product, probably for commercial reasons. Finally, human insulin products of one Indian manufacturer were refused by EMA due to non-compliant pharmaceutical quality and GMP objections with no clinical objections, as a hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic clamp equivalence study and two Phase 3 studies were accepted.

The basis of these approvals is studies using the hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic clamp technique. In a preferably double-blind cross-over design, single subcutaneous doses of the biosimilar and reference insulins are applied. The blood glucose is maintained ('clamped') at a pre-defined level by means of a variable infusion of glucose. The Glucose Infusion Rate (GIR) profile reflects the pharmacodynamic effect of the insulin, and frequent blood samples are taken to establish the pharmacokinetic profile. An insulin-sensitive study population is required to best detect potential product-related differences. For short or intermediate-acting insulin, this could be either healthy volunteers or C-peptide negative people with type 1 diabetes. In studies with healthy volunteers, the target clamp level is usually slightly below the fasting glucose to prevent interference by endogenous insulin secretion. For people with type 1 diabetes, 100 mg/dL is the typical target plasma glucose clamp level. For comparison of long-acting insulins, patients with T1DM are preferable in order to exclude any interference with endogenous insulin secretion. In clamp studies, a relatively high insulin dose is used to ensure a pharmacodynamic response. Both EMA and FDA require respective EU and US reference products to be compared head-to-head to the biosimilar under investigation. Thus, three-way clamp studies with an EU reference, US reference, and investigational biosimilar insulin can meet the requirements of both agencies in one study.

Both agencies agree on the primary pharmacokinetic endpoints, AUC(0-t) and C max, and pharmacodynamic endpoints, GIR-AUC(0-t) and GIRmax. Also, the acceptance criteria for pharmacokinetic endpoints to conclude on biosimilarity are identical for EMA and FDA: the 90% confidence interval of the point estimate (the ratio between biosimilar and reference insulin) should be between 80% and 125%. However, the acceptance criteria for the pharmacodynamic endpoints differ; FDA requires the 90% confidence interval and EMA the 95% CI to be between 80% and 125%, EMA thus being more strict.

The hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic clamp study can either be performed manually or automated. During manual clamps, blood samples for glucose measurements are drawn (usually every 5-10 min) and the investigator adapts the glucose infusion rate based on his or her experience. During automated clamps, glucose measurements are done continuously, and an algorithm adapts the glucose infusion rate every minute. For the first approved biosimilar insulin, the Eli Lilly glargine product in 2014, six clamp studies were performed, five with manual and one with automated clamps. For all other approvals, only one pivotal clamp study with automated clamps was done (Table 1). All these clamp studies confirmed biosimilarity.

Clinical efficacy and immunogenicity safety studies

Unlike for other biosimilar products, there is no absolute need for longer-term clinical studies for biosimilar insulins. Clinical efficacy phase 3 studies, the mainstay for approval of innovator drugs, are only considered supportive for biosimilars, as the safety and efficacy of the product have already been shown for the originator. In addition, as the EMA guideline on biosimilar insulins puts it, the endpoints, usually HbA1c, used in clinical efficacy studies 'are not considered sensitive enough to detect potentially clinically relevant differences between two insulins'. Indeed, while there are examples of glucose clamp studies showing differences between two insulin preparations (e.g., insulin glulisine and insulin lispro) that were not confirmed in clinical efficacy studies, there is not a single example of differences that were only seen in clinical efficacy studies, but not in glucose clamp studies. Consistently, none of the phase 3 studies that have been done for all approved biosimilar insulins (Table 2) indicated meaningful differences between the biosimilar and originator insulin, regarding HbA1c, hypoglycaemia and safety.

While the power of such clinical studies might be insufficient to compare clinical efficacy endpoints, including hypoglycaemia, or to detect differences in the adverse event profile, phase 3 studies might be used to provide data on the immunogenicity of the biological product. However, both EMA and FDA allow such studies to be waived, provided biosimilarity can convincingly be concluded from the results of the comparative analytical and functional (pre-clinical) studies as well as the clamp study. This might be surprising considering the previously mentioned unavoidable minor differences between biosimilar and reference insulins. Could differences in, for example, impurities not lead to differences in the insulin-antibody response? However, in contrast to other biologicals with a larger and more complex molecular structure, the clinical relevance of different immunogenicity characteristics (anti-drug antibody formation) of insulin products is doubtful. While studies with impure, non-genetically engineered insulins showed high antibody responses affecting insulin pharmacokinetics, newer studies were unable to demonstrate any impact of insulin antibodies on safety or efficacy findings. Therefore, there are good reasons that biosimilar insulins can be approved without large phase 3 clinical trials but just based on preclinical data and the results of glucose clamp studies. This is equivalent to the approval of generic drugs, which is mainly based on the demonstration of pharmacokinetic bioequivalence.
Interchangeability

In Europe, the EMA judges approved biosimilars to be interchangeable, but how interchangeability is implemented (whether substitution is allowed at the pharmacy level with no or limited involvement of the physician) is left to the individual countries. A 2019 FDA guidance detailed how interchangeability could be shown with a switching study, but a 2024 draft guidance considers the risk of switches insignificant, and applicants may now apply for the interchangeable designation based on modern analytical technologies and the demonstration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic bioequivalence.
Conclusion

A clear regulatory framework ensures the efficacy and safety of biosimilar insulins in Europe and the US (and many other countries not considered in this review). This regulatory framework is based on scientific evidence that the demonstration of similar physico-chemical properties and biological activity in preclinical studies and of pharmacological bioequivalence in glucose clamp studies is sufficient to make sure that the minor differences in the formulations between biosimilar and reference insulins are not of clinical relevance. Given the high standards applied, people with diabetes and prescribers can use biosimilar insulins without any concerns.

passages.text: Advancing the Identification of Bioactive Molecules and the Construction of a Synergistic Drug Delivery System in Combating Lung Injury
Abstract

In recent years, pneumonia caused by multiple viruses has posed a significant threat to public health, particularly affecting vulnerable populations such as the elderly and immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments primarily focused on antiviral medications, lacking "miracle cure" and innovative approaches for the pathological damage caused by viruses. Since 2019, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has shown remarkable efficacy in treating coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). However, the application is hindered by intricate mechanisms, variable quality, and slow onset. Clinically, Ge-Gen Decoction (GGD) effectively reduced the severity in patients with viral infections. Taking COVID-19 as a case, the bioactive ingredients from GGD: glabridin (GLA) and puerarin (PUE) are identified. Interestingly, it was discovered that PUE can self-assemble into a 3D hydrogel structure upon heating and cooling, namely PUE@gel. This process mirrored the formation of gel-like precipitates in GGD post-decoction. Motivated by this phenomenon, a decoction-mimicking drug delivery system, glabridin puerarin self-assembled hydrogel (GLA-PUE@gel) was constructed, which exhibits strong anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, comparable to GGD at the same dosage. Additionally, PUE that has a high biosafety threshold can competitively bind to angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) on host cells, preventing SARS-CoV-2 from invading. This study offered a promising approach for treating virus-induced lung injury.

Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), while holistic and historically esteemed, faces challenges in "miracle cures" due to slow onset, long cycles, and difficulty controlling quality. This study obtains the active ingredients, glabridin (GLA) and puerarin (PUE), from Ge-Gen Decoction (GGD), developing a safe and effective drug delivery system, GLA-PUE@gel, with significant potential to reduce severe lung injury in clinical settings.
Introduction

Viral pneumonia is an interstitial lung inflammation caused by the invasion of the virus into pulmonary epithelial cells through the respiratory tract. Its pathogenesis is often related to inflammatory storms and oxidative stress. Under normal circumstances, symptoms of viral pneumonia are mild and self-limiting, but severe cases can lead to sepsis, hypercapnia, hypoxemia, acute respiratory failure, circulatory system failure, and even pose a threat to life. In particular, highly contagious and fatal viral pneumonia, if not prevented and controlled promptly, can lead to significant public health incidents, causing long-term and sustained negative impacts on social and economic operations. Since the discovery of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients in December 2019, the outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 had spread to more than 200 countries, and the World Health Organization (WHO) had classified it as a global pandemic. In recent years, "three-in-one epidemic" (COVID-19, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus) of concurrent outbreaks had a significant impact on the elderly population. Due to the weakened immune systems, they were more susceptible to severe illness. For thousands of years, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) had played an important role in the prevention and treatment of epidemic diseases, and showed the remarkable characteristic advantages. The National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China had launched a treatment plan with Chinese medicine and found that it had significant effects on anti-virus, anti-inflammatory, and alleviating the symptoms of COVID-19 patients.

Ge-Gen Decoction (GGD) originated from "Treatise on Coldness-induced Diseases", which was a typical pungent-warm relieving agent and was often used to treat exogenous wind-cold exterior syndrome. GGD has demonstrated good clinical efficacy in treating upper respiratory tract diseases caused by viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus. Referring to the ancient books of TCM such as "Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic" and "Treatise on Coldness-induced Diseases", it has been postulated that GGD may be efficacious in the clinical management of COVID-19, with promising therapeutic outcomes reported. Furthermore, affirming its contemporary relevance and potential utility, the Health Commission of Shandong Province has formally integrated GGD into the strategic treatment guidelines for combating COVID-19, as of December 2022. Significantly, GanCao (Glycyrrhiza uralensis Fisch) and GeGen (Pueraria lobata (Willd.) Ohwi) in GGD stood out as a pivotal medicinal combination, demonstrating the capacity to notably diminish the risk of severe outcomes in patients afflicted with COVID-19. Puerarin (PUE), one of the main active ingredients in GeGen, had been reported to possess potent antiviral properties. It exhibited inhibitory effects against SARS-CoV-2 by interfering with binding of viral S-protein and human angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), thereby preventing the virus from entering host cells. Furthermore, it may alleviate inflammation and modulate the host's immune response to improve virus-induced lung injury. In treating influenza, GGD exhibited notable efficacy by reducing H1N1 viral titers in vivo, demonstrating significant anti-influenza A virus activity. It also reduced tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) expression, improving T-helper 1/T-helper 2 (Th1/Th2) immune balance to regulate the body's immune response. Additionally, GGD promoted the nuclear translocation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), enhancing transcription and expression of downstream antioxidant enzymes, thereby displaying potent antioxidant effects. For the treatment of respiratory syncytial virus, GGD can inhibit plaque formation by promoting the secretion of interferon-beta and preventing the virus from adhering to respiratory epithelium, thereby reducing virus-induced pathological damage. TCM, while holistic and historically esteemed, often grappled with the challenge of pinpointing a "miracle cure", beset by factors such as slow onset, long cycle, and difficulty in controlling quality. Harnessing the potent active ingredients from Chinese medicines and refining them into a "miracle drug" could indeed represent an efficacious approach to counteracting the inflammation and oxidative stress triggered by virus.

We have sought and developed safe and efficient anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agents from TCM through a multidisciplinary strategy encompassing bibliometrics, bioinformatics, pharmacology, pharmaceutics, and toxicology. This initiative is designed to offer valuable insights for the amelioration of viral-induced lung injury.
Results
Frontier and Hot Topics of TCM in Treating COVID-19
Web of Science (WOS) is a widely recognized comprehensive academic information platform. We obtained 681 records of TCM against COVID-19 in WOS, and analyzed the data by CiteSpace 6.1.6 software.

We conducted analyses of countries and regions, institutions, and author collaboration networks, as well as keyword co-occurrence, cluster themes, timelines, and citation bursts to examine the research hotspots and trends in the treatment of COVID-19 with TCM. The People's Republic of China showed the highest level of engagement, publishing 142 articles, with India and the USA also demonstrating significant interest. However, the scope of international collaboration was limited, exhibiting a certain degree of regionality, and there was a need for expanded cooperation among different countries (Figure  1A; Table S1, Supporting Information). Furthermore, the China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, and Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine ranked at the forefront in terms of their focus on TCM for COVID-19 treatment. Nevertheless, the collaboration among research institutions was narrow, with a regional bias, indicating a potential for enhanced partnerships (Figure 1B; Table S2, Supporting Information). We conducted a visual analysis of the authors (Figure 1C), and calculated the minimum number of articles published by the core authors, as calculated by Price Equation, was given by the Equation (1): where M represented the minimum number of articles published by the authors, and Nmax  was the number of articles published by the most prolific author.

Frontier and hot topics of TCM in treating COVID-19. A) Collaboration network of TCM anti-COVID-19 related articles publishing countries and regions. B) Collaboration network of TCM anti-COVID-19 related articles publishing institutions. C) Author cooperation network of TCM anti-COVID-19 related articles. D) Keywords co-occurrence network of TCM anti-COVID-19 related articles. E) Keywords clustering themes of TCM anti-COVID-19 related articles. F) Keywords timelines of TCM anti-COVID-19 related articles. G) Keywords with the strongest citation bursts.

The study found that the number of core authors in the field of TCM treatment of COVID-19 was not less than 3, and 48 core authors were identified, accounting for 20.96% of the total number of authors. The top ten core authors, in terms of articles count, were as follows: Fang Bangjiang (11), Tong Xiaolin (11), Zhang Ying (11), Wang Yu (9), Liu Qingquan (9), Zhang Han (9), Zhang Wen (7), Li Jing (7), Lian Fengmei (7), and Zhang Lei (7). According to Table S3 (Supporting Information), several collaborative teams have been established, centered around Zhang Lei, Liu Qingquan, Wang Yu, and Fang Bangjiang, indicating close internal cooperation within these groups.

Pruning was set as pathfinder, pruning sliced networks and pruning the merged network, and the data was analyzed to construct the keyword co-occurrence map (Figure 1D; Table S4, Supporting Information). Here, a total of 169 keywords were obtained, including 16 important keywords (centrality >= 0.1) (values in parentheses: the former represents centrality, and the latter represents frequency): Traditional Chinese Medicine (0.27, 29), protein (0.19, 10), acute lung injury (0.18, 12), cytokine storm (0.18, 6), SARS (0.17, 7), coronavirus disease 2019 (0.17, 6), in vitro (0.16, 6), molecular docking (0.15, 19), COVID-19 (0.13, 23), activation (0.13, 9), apoptosis (0.12, 5), medicinal plant (0.12, 2), antiviral activity (0.11, 3), coronavirus (0.1, 9), infection (0.1, 7), and main protease (0.1, 2). All keywords can be summarized into four categories: research themes (2), research methods (2), diseases and symptoms (6), and outcome indicators (6). Cluster analysis of the keywords was performed (Figure 1E), retaining the top 11 clusters: Traditional Chinese Medicines, Traditional Chinese Medicine, COVID-19, acute lung injury, molecular docking, endoribonuclease, molecular dynamics simulation, coronavirus disease 2019, NLRP3 inflammasome, Chinese herbal medicine, and professional quality of life. The cluster Q value was 0.6531, and the S value was 0.8409, indicating reliable clustering. In addition, a timeline analysis of the keywords was conducted, revealing that drug-drug interaction, care, anti-SARS-CoV-2 drug, Xuanbai Chengqi Decoction, biology, amygdalin, NLRP3 inflammasome, macrophage polarization, injury, and antiviral drugs were at the forefront of research keywords (Figure 1F). Finally, the burst words that increase sharply in a short period of time can be found in a specific year, so as to reveal the duration and trend of the hot topics. As shown in Figure 1G, terms such as "coronavirus", "SARS", "in vitro", and "decoction" exhibit high burst strength, while terms like "metabolism", "SARS-CoV-2", "model", "randomized controlled trial", "pharmacology", "component", "inhibitor" remain as hot topics in the research on TCM's treatment of COVID-19 in recent years. Therefore, it was imperative to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of TCM in treating COVID-19 and other viral diseases.
Molecular Mechanism of GanCao GeGen in Treating COVID-19
GanCao GeGen was identified as an effective Chinese herbal pair for the treatment of COVID-19. However, its molecular mechanism was still unclear.

First, we collected 101 potential active ingredients from GanCao GeGen, predicted and obtained 756 ingredient-targets and 601 disease-targets, of which 30 were the intersection targets of GanCao GeGen in the treatment of COVID-19 (Figure  2A). Then, a PPI network between targets was constructed on the STRING 12.0 platform to further get core targets (Figure 2B,C): Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), tumor necrosis factor (TNF), vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA), mechanistic target of rapamycin (MTOR), estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1), integrin subunit beta 1 (ITGB1), and tank-binding kinase 1 (TBK1). In addition, we conducted Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis on the Metascape 3.5 platform (Figure 2D,E). All items were sorted from small to large according to p value, and the related biological process (BP) included cell activation, leukocyte activation, lymphocyte activation, regulation of protein kinase B signaling, inflammatory response, positive regulation of protein kinase B signaling, protein phosphorylation, viral life cycle, cellular response to organic cyclic compound, and response to hormone. The related cellular components (CC) included membrane raft, membrane microdomain, lysosome, lytic vacuole, vesicle lumen, vacuolar lumen, endolysosome, ficolin-1-rich granule lumen, secretory granule lumen, and cytoplasmic vesicle lumen. The related molecular functions (MF) included kinase activity, phosphotransferase activity, alcohol group as acceptor, protein kinase activity, protein serine/threonine kinase activity, fibronectin binding, protein serine/threonine/tyrosine kinase activity, proteoglycan binding, protease binding, collagen binding, virus receptor activity. The related signaling pathways included proteoglycans in cancer, human papillomavirus infection, pathways in cancer, human cytomegalovirus infection, autophagy-animal, endocrine resistance, chemical carcinogenesis-receptor activation, thyroid hormone signaling pathway, platelet activation, shigellosis, apelin signaling pathway, fluid shear stress and atherosclerosis, phospholipase D signaling pathway, longevity regulating pathway-multiple species, pancreatic cancer, EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance, PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus infection, Epstein-Barr virus infection, PD-L1 expression and PD-1 checkpoint pathway in cancer (Table S5, Supporting Information). It was evident that these signaling pathways were involved in a variety of viral diseases, suggesting that GGD may have a broad-spectrum efficacy in treating viral infections. Additionally, we found that phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) and protein kinase B (Akt) exhibited strong genetic correlations with the core targets, suggesting that the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway may be a key mechanism in GGD's treatment of COVID-19 (Figure S1A,B, Supporting Information). These signaling pathways were accompanied by changes in ROS levels, and since the Nrf2 signaling pathway was a classic pathway for oxidative stress, we also confirmed that Nrf2 and the antioxidant enzyme glutathione reductase (GR) have strong genetic correlations with the core targets, indicating a significant association with ROS (Figure S1C,D, Supporting Information). Finally, we constructed an ingredient target disease network, showing the "holistic view" of GanCao GeGen in treating COVID-19 (Figure 2F).

The eligible GSE160435 dataset was screened in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, and the core target was input into the dataset for verification, and the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was drawn (Figure 2G). ROC curve quantified the diagnostic efficacy of a model by measuring its sensitivity and specificity across a range of threshold values. The area under concentration-time (AUC) served as a comprehensive metric for the diagnostic accuracy of models. AUC scores above 0.5 had predictive value, above 0.7 indicated good diagnostic value, and above 0.9 indicated high diagnostic value. As shown in Figure 2H, the AUC scores of EGFR, ITGB1, TBK1, TNF, and VEGFA were all above 0.7, and the AUC scores of ITGB1 and TNF were more than 0.9, indicating that the diagnostic value of these targets was higher in the process of COVID-19. Additionally, the expression of ITGB1 and TNF in the disease group was significantly higher than that in the control group, and TNF, as a key indicator of inflammation, was closely related to COVID-19. Thus, TNF may be the key targets of GanCao GeGen in the treatment of COVID-19.
Glabridin (GLA) and Puerarin (PUE) as Candidate Drugs in Treating COVID-19

It was reported that ACE2, 3C-likeprotease (3CL pro), Papain-like protease (Plp), and TNF were the key targets in the treatment of COVID-19, and the binding ability of the key targets to active ingredients in GanCao GeGen was verified by computer modeling.

The accuracy of protein crystal structures determined the precision of computer modeling, and the modeling results were assessed through SAVES 6.0. The Ramachandran plot was a visualization method that described whether the dihedral angles psi and phi of amino acid residues in the protein structure were within reasonable regions, and it can also reflect whether the conformation of the protein was rational. For ACE2, 93.3% of the amino acids were situated in the most favored regions, 6.7% were found in the allowed regions, with no amino acids present in the generously allowed or disallowed regions. Thus, 100% of the amino acids were within the rational regions. For 3CL pro, 90.6% of the amino acids were in the most favored regions, 8.7% were in the allowed regions, 0.4% were in the generously allowed regions, and 0.4% were in the disallowed regions, leading to 99.6% of the amino acids being within the rational regions. For Plp, 88.0% of the amino acids were in the most favored regions, 10.2% were in the allowed regions, 1.8% were in the generously allowed regions, and none were in the disallowed regions, which meant 100% of the amino acids were within the rational regions. For TNF, 90.2% of the amino acids were in the most favored regions, 9.6% were in the allowed regions, 0.2% were in the generously allowed regions, and again, none were in the disallowed regions, resulting in 100% of the amino acids being within the rational regions (Figure  3A). In addition, we have identified the precise values of ACE2, 3CL pro, Plp, and TNF protein crystal structures to be 96.9336, 96.5517, 91.5612, and 96.4989, respectively, indicating that these 3D protein structure models were reliable (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

Given that TNF-alpha was identified in the preceding systemic network analysis, the HipHop algorithm was employed to valid the binding affinity of GLA and PUE to TNF-alpha. We identified six active compounds with strong TNF-alpha inhibitory activity: Japonicone A, AP-906/41640035, SPD-304, EJMC-1, Erythrosine B, and Quercetin, which constituted the training set (Figure S3, Supporting Information). This resulted in the generation of ten pharmacophore models, each comprising three feature elements (Table S6, Supporting Information). Evaluation of compounds alignment with pharmacophore models revealed that the FitValue ranking of pharmacophore model 05 closely correlated with the IC50 values of active compounds. The compatibility of GLA and PUE with pharmacophore model 05, and their FitValue ranked just below that of AP-906/41640035, suggesting their potential strong inhibitory activity against TNF-alpha (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

Considering the molecular docking results, the molecular dynamics simulation of ingredient key target composite systems was investigated, and the preprocessing procedure was shown in Figures S5 and S6 (Supporting Information). The stability of the system was tested by calculating the RMSD value within 20 ns simulation time, and the results were shown in Figure 3D,E. The results showed that the backbone RMSD of the GLA key target composite system tended to stabilize after 10 ns, and that of the PUE key target composite system stabilized after 15 ns, which had good stability without obvious conformational fluctuation. Then, the RMSF value of amino acid skeleton atoms of the key targets were further calculated during the molecular dynamics simulation process, and the results were shown in Figure 3F. The RMSF value indicated that the key targets had greater flexibility and movement intensity during the simulation process. Furthermore, we analyzed the hydrogen bonds of the systems, and found that the main bonding modes of GLA ACE2, GLA 3CL pro, and GLA Plp were hydrogen bonds, whereas the binding mode of GLA TNF does not primarily rely on hydrogen bonds (Figure 3G), which was consistent with the molecular docking results. Also, we found that the main bonding modes of PUE ACE2, PUE 3CL pro, PUE Plp, and GLA TNF were hydrogen bonds, especially for PUE 3CL pro and PUE TNF. The total energy change of ingredient key target composite systems was calculated, and the total energy was stable in the simulation process. The stability order of the composite systems for GLA and PUE was as follows: TNF composite systems > ACE2 composite systems > 3CL pro composite systems > Plp composite systems (Figure 3H). Importantly, we also performed energy decomposition analysis on the amino acid residues of key targets, and found that ASP30 (ACE2), THR26 (3CL pro), TYR269 (Plp), and LEU36 (TNF) contributed the most affinity to GLA, respectively (Figure 3I). Additionally, ASP30 (ACE2), GLU166 (3CL pro), GLU264 (Plp), and GLU135 (TNF) contributed the most affinity to PUE, respectively (Figure 3J). To further identify the key binding sites between the proteins and ingredients, we employed alanine scanning mutagenesis to investigate and mutate the amino acids within the active sites. The results revealed that the key binding sites for GLA with 3CL pro were ASN142 and GLN189, with ACE2 was GLN96, with Plp were LEU163 and TYR269, and with TNF were GLY148, HIS15, and LEU36 (Figure 3K; Table S7, Supporting Information). For PUE, the key binding sites with 3CL pro were GLN189, MET165, MET49, and HIS41, with ACE2 were ARG393, HIS34, and PRO389, with Plp were TYR274, LEU163, and TYR269, and with TNF were TYR119, VAL123, TYR59, LEU55, GLN61, GLY121, and TYR119 (Figure 3L; Table S8, Supporting Information).
Study on Anti-Inflammatory and Antioxidant Effects of GLA

Considering the established anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties of PUE from early research, this study did not deem further replication necessary. Morphological examination of RAW264.7 cells under normal conditions depicted them as small, round, plump, and well-defined. In contrast, LPS-induced inflammation led to a transformation in cellular morphology, characterized by the protrusion of pseudopodia and an enlargement in cell size with blurred contours. After GLA treatment on LPS-induced M1 macrophages, the number of irregularly shaped cells decreased. (Figure S7A, Supporting Information). We revealed that GLA effectively inhibited the cellular expression of inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta and TNF-alpha by Western blot (Figure S7B-D, Supporting Information). Also, we used Griess assay to determine the inhibitory effect of GLA on the secretion of nitric oxide (NO) by M1 macrophages. Preparation and Characterization of GLA-PUE@gel

GLA exhibited good antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. However, its application was limited by the strong hydrophobicity (Figure  4A). PUE contained hydrophilic glycosyl groups and hydrophobic aromatic groups (Figure 4B), which enabled a balance between molecular solubility in water and the ability to self-assemble. A decoction-mimicking hydrogel of PUE can be synthesized via a heating-cooling method. Under high supersaturation conditions, the gelation process of PUE began with nucleation, followed by rapid fiber growth radiating from the nucleation centers. As supersaturation increased, the type of fiber growth shifts from a "fibrillar" pattern to a "non-linear" one, resulting in a denser structure with higher fractal dimensions and enhanced mechanical properties.

In this study, we developed a glabridin-puerarin self-assembled hydrogel (GLA-PUE@gel) with a decoction-mimicking preparation method. Figure 4C illustrated the macroscopic morphology of the hydrogel, demonstrating its integrity and uniformity. Additionally, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was employed to characterize PUE@gel and GLA-PUE@gel, revealing the highly interconnected porous network at different magnifications (Figure 4D). The smoothness of the pore walls and the interconnectivity between pores can be observed, particularly at higher magnifications. Compared to PUE@gel, GLA-PUE@gel exhibited smaller pore sizes and thicker pore walls under the same magnification. DSC curve was shown in Figure 4E. GLA exhibited an endothermic peak at  230.9  C. PUE showed an endothermic peak at  95.2  C due to the loss of crystalline water, and its melting point appeared at 203.3  C. The physical mixture of GLA/PUE displayed an endothermic peak at  95.9  C due to the loss of crystalline water, with a melting point at 202.5  C, possibly indicating a lower GLA content. The glass transition temperature (Tg) of PUE@gel was 71.4  C, indicating that PUE may exist in an amorphous form after being prepared into a hydrogel. GLA-PUE@gel exhibited an endothermic peak at  53.4  C, which may be associated with a new amorphous form upon the incorporation of GLA. As reported, the characteristic peaks of GLA in X-ray Diffraction (XRD) were identified at 2theta values of 16.15  and 17.73 . From Figure S8 (Supporting Information), it was found that the characteristic peaks of GLA were present in PUE@gel+GLA, whereas they were absent in GLA-PUE@gel, indicating the formation of a new co-gel system. Furthermore, dynamic time sweep tests were performed on PUE@gel and GLA-PUE@gel at 1% strain and 1 rad s-1 frequency. The storage modulus (G') was found to be significantly higher than the loss modulus (G''), as shown in Figure 4F, confirming the formation of the hydrogel.

Subsequently, we simulated the in vivo degradation process of GLA-PUE@gel, revealing complete degradation at  12 h (Figure 4G). Furthermore, we simulated the in vivo release behaviors of GLA and PUE in GLA-PUE@gel, showing consistent cumulative release percentages at different time points (Figure 4H). Model fitting indicated that the release behaviors of GLA and PUE followed a Zero-order model, with 0.45 < n < 0.89, and n values approaching 0.89 (Table  2 ). The degradation percentage was linearly fitted with the cumulative GLA and PUE release (R 2 > 0.99), indicating a strong linear relationship (Figure 4I). This suggested that the release of GLA and PUE was primarily controlled by the degradation of the hydrogel matrix, with drug diffusion playing a secondary role. Importantly, we obtained the concentration ratios of PUE:GLA at different times during the release process and calculated an average of 29.21:1 (mol mol-1), closely matching the initial preparation ratio of 30:1 (mol mol-1) (Figure 4J). According to DSC and XRD results, it was found that GLA and PUE interacted with each other in GLA-PUE@gel, forming a new co-gel system that enabled nearly synchronous release of both compounds. This indicated that the decoction-mimicking drug delivery system may maintain a stable release ratio in vivo, ensuring therapeutic efficacy.

The Mechanistic Understanding of Self-Assembled Hydrogel Formation

In this section, we followed the preparation concentration of PUE@gel: 92.46 mM (PUE). We constructed a 15 x 15 x 15 nm3 SPC water model box and added 180 PUE molecules to investigate the self-assembly capability under specific conditions (Figure S10, Supporting Information). Through self-assembly simulation experiments, we gained an understanding of the mechanism behind the formation of PUE@gel: 180 PUE gradually aggregated within 20 ns, exhibiting a porous structure (Figure  5A). Furthermore, the RMSD and energy of PUE and its system stabilized during the formation of the self-assembled hydrogel (Figure 5B,C), with hydrogen bonding and pi-pi stacking being among the primary driving forces (Figure 5D,E).

Building upon previous findings, it was established that GLA and PUE were key active ingredients in GGD, displaying significant synergistic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. However, the mechanism of action remained unclear. Following the preparation ratio of GLA-PUE@gel: 3.08 mM (GLA) and 92.46 mM (PUE), we constructed a cubic box with a side length of 15 nm and formed an SPC water model system. We then added 180 PUE and 6 GLA molecules to the system (Figure S11, Supporting Information), calculating the quantities of ingredients based on the following Equation (5): where N is the amount of substance in moles, C is the concentration of the substance in solution, V is the volume of the solution, NA  is Avogadro constant.

Through self-assembly simulation experiments, we gained an understanding of the mechanism behind the formation of GLA-PUE@gel: 6 GLA and 180 PUE gradually aggregated within 20 ns, exhibiting a porous structure (Figure 5F). RMSD of the system, PUE, and GLA reached a steady state after  12 ns (Figure 5G). After 10 ns, the amount of hydrogen bonds between PUE PUE tended to be in a stable state, which may be related to the participation of GLA (Figure 5H). GLA was enveloped within PUE@gel through hydrogen bonding and pi-pi stacking, forming GLA-PUE@gel (Figure 5I,K). Additionally, the energy of the system ranged from -4.46 to -4.47 x 10-6 kJ mol-1, indicating that GLA cannot significantly affect the overall energy change of the system (Figure 5J). Docking results revealed that the binding affinity of PUE PUE was slightly stronger than that of GLA PUE (Figure 5E,K; Tables S9 and S10, Supporting Information), both being less than -5 kcal mol-1, indicating that the interaction force between individual molecules was weak, while the spatial structure of multiple molecules was the main contributor for the stability of the system.
Study on the Anti-Inflammatory and Antioxidant Effects of GLA-PUE@gel

To determine the synergistic anti-inflammatory proportion of GLA/PUE, we employed the Griess assay to measure the changes in NO levels in macrophage culture supernatants. First, we confirmed that GLA exhibited significant anti-inflammatory effects at doses above 0.4 microM (Figure  6A). Subsequently, we established concentration gradients of GLA:PUE ratios at 1:10, 1:20, 1:30, and 1:40, while ensuring that GLA and PUE remained within safe dosage ranges. Notably, the ratio of GLA to PUE at 1:30 was found to be particularly effective in eliciting a pronounced anti-inflammatory response (Figure 6B). Based on this finding, we prepared GLA-PUE@gel and compared its anti-inflammatory activity with free drugs and GGD. We found that GLA-PUE@gel showed significant differences in anti-inflammatory activity compared to GLA, PUE, and GGD, but no significant difference compared to the GLA/PUE, indicating a rational synergistic proportion (Figure 6C,D). Furthermore, we investigated the impact of GLA-PUE@gel on the levels of IL-1beta in macrophages and observed a significant reduction in IL-1beta levels compared to the LPS group (Figure 6E). Changes in surface markers on macrophages were important indicators for assessing inflammatory and non-inflammatory states. We induced an inflammatory model (M1) using LPS and an anti-inflammatory model (M2) using IL-4. After treating M1 macrophages with GLA-PUE@gel for 24 h, we observed a significant decrease in the proportion of CD86-positive macrophages and an increase in the proportion of CD206-positive macrophages (Figure 6F). This indicated that GLA-PUE@gel can reprogram the inflammatory state of macrophages into a non-inflammatory state, thereby inhibiting the release of inflammatory factors.

To determine the antioxidant effect of GLA-PUE@gel, we constructed a cellular oxidative stress model using H2O2. Initially, we treated human alveolar basal epithelial cells (A549) with 400 microM H2O2 and measured cell viability after 2 h and 4 h. It was observed that cell viability was reduced to  50% after a 4-h exposure to 400 microM H2O2, indicating successful induction of oxidative stress model. However, GLA-PUE@gel significantly attenuated oxidative stress damage (Figure 6G). Furthermore, we assessed the impact of GLA-PUE@gel on reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels using an ELISA assay kit. H2DCFDA was inherently non-fluorescent and can freely penetrate cell membranes. Once inside the cell, it was hydrolyzed by cellular esterases to form DCFH, which was not membrane-permeable, thus allowing the probe to be easily loaded into the cells. Subsequently, non-fluorescent DCFH can be oxidized by intracellular ROS to form fluorescent DCF. Immunofluorescence (Figure 6H,I) and flow cytometry (Figure 6J) were utilized to detect the fluorescence intensity of DCF and assess intracellular ROS levels. The results demonstrated that GLA-PUE@gel significantly reduced intracellular ROS levels, indicating remarkable antioxidant activity.

Excessive ROS can disrupt the normal function of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), such as protein folding and quality control processes, thereby inducing ER stress. Further investigations revealed that GLA-PUE@gel activated the expression of C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), which in turn inhibited apoptosis of cells (Figure 6K). Under ER stress conditions, calreticulin (CRT) can translocate from the ER to the cell membrane, thereby inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoting T cells to produce large amounts of cytokines, and exacerbating inflammation. GLA-PUE@gel effectively suppressed this process, suggesting its potential in alleviating oxidative stress damage through inhibition of the ER stress pathway (Figure 6L). Moreover, overexpression of high mobility group box 1 protein (HMGB1) can induce ER stress in A549 cells, and GLA-PUE@gel can significantly reduce the production of HMGB1 (Figure 6M).

In previous studies, it was found that PUE can inhibit the production of inflammatory factors to reduce inflammation and oxidative stress damage, while GLA can reprogram M1 macrophages into M2 macrophages, thereby exerting anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. ACE2 was a zinc metalloproteinase, which belonged to type I transmembrane protein. It was originally thought to be expressed in the heart, kidney and testis, and later found to be widely expressed in the lung, brain and digestive tract. Studies have found that ACE2 was a key membrane receptor for SARS-CoV-2 entering host cells and had a strong binding ability to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor binding domain (RBD). It has been reported that PUE can competitively inhibit the binding of ACE2 and RBD, thereby preventing SARS-CoV-2 from entering host cells. Using computer simulation technology, we discovered that PUE can competitively occupy the active binding sites of ACE2 and RBD (GLU35, GLU37, LYS353, ARG393), thus preventing SARS-CoV-2 from binding to host cells (Figure 6N; Table S11, Supporting Information). The synergistic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects of GLA and PUE have been demonstrated to markedly reduce the pathological damage induced by SARS-CoV-2. This insight shed light on the mechanism by which GLA-PUE@gel exerted its therapeutic efficacy, highlighting its potential as a novel treatment approach (Figure 6O).
GLA-PUE@gel Alleviates Acute Lung Injury (ALI) in Mice

To evaluate the anti-inflammatory and antioxidant stress capabilities of GLA-PUE@gel, we employed a mouse model of ALI, as illustrated in Figure  7A (the details are provided in the Experimental Section). Macroscopic examination revealed that the lungs of the ALI group exhibited significant swelling with a red-and-white mottled appearance (Figure S12A, Supporting Information). Additionally, the spleens of the ALI group showed marked enlargement and darkening in color, whereas GLA-PUE@gel treatment significantly ameliorated these pathological changes (Figure S12B, Supporting Information). To quantitatively assess pulmonary edema, lungs were dried at 80  C for 48 h to obtain dry weights, and the wet-to-dry weight ratio was calculated. Furthermore, lung and spleen indices were determined to evaluate the degree of lung consolidation and systemic immune function, respectively. The results demonstrated that GLA-PUE@gel significantly alleviated pulmonary edema and reduced both lung and spleen indices (Figure 7B-D), indicating its protective effects against lung consolidation and its ability to modulate immune function. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of 50 mg kg-1 GLA-PUE@gel surpassed that of a clinically equivalent dose of GGD, particularly in reducing the lung index, where a statistically significant difference was observed. Histopathological analysis via H&E staining revealed that normal lung tissues exhibited thin and intact alveolar walls, clear alveolar spaces without exudate, uniform interstitium without thickening or inflammatory cell infiltration, and no significant pathological alterations. In contrast, ALI lung tissues displayed markedly thickened alveolar walls, collapsed or fused alveolar spaces, and abundant pink proteinaceous exudate and red blood cells within the alveolar cavities. Additionally, extensive infiltration of inflammatory cells, such as neutrophils and macrophages, was observed in both the alveolar spaces and interstitium. The interstitium was significantly thickened, accompanied by edema and inflammatory cell aggregation, resulting in disrupted lung architecture and characteristic features of acute inflammation and injury. However, GLA-PUE@gel effectively ameliorated these histopathological changes in ALI (Figure 7E).

To further validate the observed experimental phenomena, we assessed inflammation and oxidative stress-related markers in lung tissues from each group. Immunohistochemical analysis of TNF-alpha expression revealed low levels in normal lung tissues, whereas ALI lungs exhibited significantly elevated TNF-alpha expression, reflecting a robust inflammatory response and the pivotal role of TNF-alpha in lung injury. Notably, GLA-PUE@gel treatment markedly reduced TNF-alpha levels in lung tissues (Figure 7F). Additionally, flow cytometry was employed to evaluate changes in the proportions of CD86+ and CD206+ macrophages in lung tissues. The percentage of CD86+ macrophages in ALI lungs was significantly higher than in the normal group, reaching 27.8%. In contrast, treatment groups, particularly the GLA-PUE@gel group, significantly reduced the proportion of CD86+ macrophages while increasing the proportion of CD206+ macrophages (Figure 7G-I). Finally, flow cytometry was used to assess changes in ROS levels in lung tissues. The results demonstrated that GLA-PUE@gel treatment significantly reduced ROS levels in lung tissues (Figure 7J,K).
Preliminary Assessment of Drug-Like Properties and Biological Safety

In the drug-likeness evaluation of GLA and PUE, we found that PUE had a low GI absorption, indicating that the free drug may not be suitable for direct oral administration; PUE had poor BBB permeability, suggesting that the free drug may not be suitable for central nervous system diseases; PUE was not a P-gp substrate, indicating that it may not be recognized and pumped out of cells by P-gp; PUE was not a CYP1A2 inhibitor, CYP2C19 inhibitor, CYP2C9 inhibitor, CYP2D6 inhibitor, or CYP3A4 inhibitor, suggesting that it may not affect drug metabolism inside cells; PUE complied with Lipinski and Ghose rules, indicating a certain degree of drug-likeness; PUE had an LD50 of 832 mg kg-1 in animals with no significant toxicity to the body, suggesting high safety (Figure  8A,B; Table S12, Supporting Information).
